A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GABI research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference experiments on heat, airfoil flow, car resonance/source localization and terrain flow, including numerical comparisons in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports channel-width sensitivity and out-of-distribution airfoil results.

M1.justification: The geometry-conditioned autoencoder, reconstruction-plus-MMD objective, Gaussian latent prior, ABC/NUTS inference and joint noise estimation remain unchanged. Added explanations and corrected indices do not establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: The four original application domains remain. Appendix B.4.2 adds evaluation on ten out-of-distribution airfoil geometries, extending the tested input population beyond the original airfoil setting.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain the same comparator membership, including Direct Map and GP Matérn 1/2, Matérn 3/2 and RBF where applicable. The new width study compares the already evaluated ABC and NUTS samplers; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: New protocols include varying channel width while fixing latent dimension at 100, and testing ten outlier airfoils using 20 pressure observations. Geometric departure is assessed through Mahalanobis distance using nine shape statistics. The original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's latent-dimension and architecture comparisons, v2 adds a channel-width ablation measuring accuracy, coverage and runtime (Figure 9), and an explicit geometry-shift robustness study (Figure 13). These substantially extend the analyses to model-capacity sensitivity and failures outside the training distribution.

E5.justification: Mean-plus/minus reporting, plot error bars and one-/two-standard-deviation coverage reporting retain their existing practices. The note that GABI-NUTS was tested for 100 rather than 1,000 runs is unchanged. No new seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the retained plots preserve their results. New Figure 9 reports width-dependent accuracy, coverage and timing; Figure 13 adds outlier pressure MAEs of 0.065–0.229 and two-standard-deviation coverage of 53–100%. These results concern additional experimental settings.

T1.justification: Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.3 and their proofs retain their mathematical substance. The expanded empirical-measure notation and explicit noise-prior factorization restate existing mathematics; the product-prior assumption already appears in v1 Appendix A.3.

C1.justification: The five listed contributions and conclusion retain the same prior-learning, posterior-equivalence, noise-estimation, predictive-performance and scalability claims. The abstract clarifies the multi-system motivation; its deleted foundation-model sentence remains represented in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies applicability to in-distribution geometries and interprets the new outlier tests as limited robustness, warning of unreliable inference from prior misspecification. It also explains location-dependent uncertainty in Figure 2 and removes Appendix C.2's rationale for preferring a regularized autoencoder over a graph VAE.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the existing car simulation's Helmholtz parameters, κ=500 and γ=0.2, clarifies timing definitions, and describes holdout reconstruction and latent-Gaussianity checks. These are documentation additions; the previously reported architectures, optimizers, training budgets and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.2.1 adds Hosseini et al. (2025), Conditional optimal transport on function spaces, to conditional inference work and removes the statement that the cited probabilistic-map works do not focus on learning priors. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a two-stage overview, expands setup and notation explanations, explains GP comparisons, and introduces an overview of the numerical section. Copyediting and removal of Appendix C.2 accompany these targeted revisions; the overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9 and 13, resizes several existing panels, revises captions, and repositions tables, figures and Algorithm 1 through page reflow. Conference headers are added. Existing table structures and underlying plot content are retained.

improvement.justification: The new width ablation and outlier tests make sensitivity and failure boundaries more assessable, while clearer exposition and disclosed Helmholtz parameters aid reproducibility. These limited gains outweigh the loss of Appendix C.2's autoencoder-versus-VAE rationale. The main benchmark evidence and theoretical contribution remain unchanged.
